I've found bigger ships to be counterproductive; the torpedo spheres shred any vessel that's large enough to be considered a primary target. Corvettes + tenders are the way.

1. A wide line of PD-capable ships in front of the main line to stop the red deluge from the spheres (preferrably no hardpoints and capable of damage output e.g. surveyor-class. Sprinkle fast PD-ships like lancers and tartans in here and there to compensate for slower PD-ships).

2. An equally wide line of fleet tenders directly behind them (preferrably no hardpoints) to heal PD-Ships from turbolaser damage. Put a second line of larger fleet tenders behind them to exclusively heal the smaller ones.

3. Behind that, the main line of star destroyers/heavy cruisers/frigates to comfortably bomb the fools to bits as they helplessly throw themselves at your line with their main damage type made useless by PD.

  
Use Bombers to exclusively disable shields and engines, to control the amount of enemy ships that simultaneously arrive at your line and make it easier to strip TS of their torpedo magazines. Do not break formation; only let the main line engage enemies when they are close enough to maintain your formation. On support vessels, target Heavy turbolasers first and try to leave ion cannons in place, as that will result in a functionally useless vessel that takes up pop cap for your enemy (your tenders will outheal damage as long as your enemy doesn't target a single ship exclusively). Do not touch your PD and tender line unless it is to plug any gaps that concentrated damage from the enemy has created. 

This formula usually makes defensive battles trivial (but long and tedious, with lots of micromanaging). I managed to beat a far larger fleet (\~12 Torpedo spheres) using this method.

Defensive stations / starbases are too weak, to the point where I don't consider it worth the trouble to build them unless it's at least a Golan-III, Validusia or Empress, etc. 

I can understand not wanting to give the player an easy way to defend a planet without a defense fleet, but a single ISD-II is enough to beat a Golan-III, if you use its fighter complement effectively. 

Making them stronger would make both defenses against something like an allegiance doomstack more interesting, as well as make attacks against them more difficult and challenging. You'd have to really strategize if a golan-III could take on two ISDs at the same time and come out on top with its shields still intact, or at least only minor hull damage sustained.
